query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: An actively learned moment tensor machine-learning potential (MTP) trained on ab initio snapshots of the high-temperature HEA liquid will serve as a superior reference for thermodynamic integration in both solid and liquid states near melting, improving reference–target phase-space overlap and reducing the integration‐path mismatch by at least 30 % compared to TOR-TILD’s EAM references.
generation.material_initial_state: Equimolar CoCrFeMnNi in both FCC solid and liquid states at temperatures near its melting point (~1700 K).
generation.intervention: Replace the TOR-TILD EAM reference with an on-the-fly active-learning moment tensor potential trained on ab initio MD configurations sampled from both liquid and solid phases.
generation.conditions: Multicomponent HEA with ≥5 elements in near-equiatomic ratios (each > 0.15), temperature range 1400–2000 K (±300 K around Tₘ).
generation.structural_mediator: Machine-learning potential capturing high-order many-body and multi-element interactions in disordered atomic configurations.
generation.mechanism: By force-matching to a diverse set of ab initio snapshots, the MTP reference spans a much larger portion of the true ab initio configuration space, yielding higher overlap with target ensembles.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermodynamic-integration path mismatch energy difference reduced by ~30–60 % (e.g. from ~10 meV/atom with EAM to ~4–7 meV/atom with MTP).
generation.baseline: TOR-TILD’s EAM references show ~10 meV/atom path mismatch for liquid and solid CoCrFeMnNi near Tₘ.
generation.boundary: Applies to equimolar HEAs of ≥5 elements at Tₘ±300 K; may not hold for alloys with strong chemical ordering or phase separation tendencies.
generation.uncertainty: ±20 % on the predicted reduction due to training-set coverage and potential extrapolation errors.

falsification_experiment.design: Compute free-energy differences for solid and liquid CoCrFeMnNi via thermodynamic integration using both the TOR-TILD EAM reference and the proposed active-learning MTP reference.
measurements: Path mismatch energy difference (meV/atom) for EAM vs. MTP
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MTP reference does not achieve at least a 30 % reduction in the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to the TOR-TILD EAM reference, the hypothesis is falsified.
